units: Adaptive Structural Evolution Boundary (ASEB): mechanics of evolvability.
Framework studies conditions allowing adaptive systems to continue evolving.
What determines whether a system can continue changing the mechanisms by which it adapts?

Evolution is constrained not only by variation but by continued feedback reception, internal structural modification, new-representation discovery and new transformation pathways; optimization can rise while evolvability falls.
Improvement: better performance within current structure; Delta A > 0; capability increases.
Evolution: structure producing capability changes; Delta Gamma > 0; generator changes.
Evolvability: preservation of ability to generate future structural changes; Delta E > 0.
A system is evolutionarily viable when feedback can reach structures determining future behavior.
P_C: whether external reality can modify the system.
P_E: whether beliefs and models can be revised.
O_C: whether the system can change categories and structures it operates over.
Adaptive boundaries determine incoming information, possible changes, modifiable structures and reachable futures.
Creation of new meaningful distinctions is proposed as prerequisite for new adaptive possibilities.
Major capability transitions are proposed to occur when structural constraints shift, changing representation, reachable computation and adaptive regime.
Goals: formal adaptive-boundary models, structural-evolution simulations, permeability metrics, phase-transition tests and optimization-vs-evolvability benchmarks.
ASEB is source-described as mechanics/conditions for remaining evolvable; Ancestor Intelligence as selection/direction toward future transformers; together lead toward open-ended evolution.
Repository is source-described as ongoing theoretical development and experimental frameworks, aiming to understand structural conditions for expanding intelligence/adaptation/evolution.
Delta A, Delta Gamma and Delta E are symbolic role labels without operational scales, estimators or common units in README.
P_C, P_E and O_C have conceptual definitions but no estimators, thresholds or aggregation rule here.
Protective-versus-evolution-blocking boundary status is posed as a question without an operational classification criterion.
Structural threshold, constraint identity and causal attribution for phase transitions are not operationalized in README.
Named Ancestor Intelligence endpoint is not resolved to an immutable corpus object and the source relation emits no map edge.
Experimental frameworks are described but the frozen repository has no code, data, run artifact or reported experiment result.
Adaptation is proposed as preserving mechanisms for future change; performance may rise while evolvability falls.
optimization -> adaptation -> structural evolution -> continued evolvability.
Evolution requires accessible feedback: adaptive differences must be detectable and reality must be able to modify internal structure.
environment -> feedback -> representation update -> structural change.
Adaptation operates through representations rather than direct access to reality.
Representation determines visible differences, detectable patterns, optimizable variables and imaginable futures.
State change Delta X, generator change Delta Gamma and evolvability Delta(Delta Gamma) are distinguished as increasing adaptation depths.
Delta X changes current state; Delta Gamma changes mechanism producing behavior; Delta(Delta Gamma) changes process by which future generators can change.
Examples range from learning/correction to new algorithms/strategies/representations and scientific methodology/education/research processes.
Boundaries determine information ingress, modifiable structures and reachable transformations.
Protective boundaries maintain stability while allowing useful adaptation; restrictive boundaries prevent structural change.
Does a boundary preserve identity while allowing evolution, or prevent evolution in order to preserve identity?
Evolution requires representation expansion: systems cannot evolve through possibilities they cannot represent.
Language, mathematics and computation are presented as representation expansions that enlarge future adaptation space.
Capability and evolvability can diverge: capability may rise while exploration, revision capacity and representation flexibility fall.
Evolutionary closure is high optimization/effectiveness with reduced openness to new evolution.
Open systems preserve correction pathways: being wrong, detecting error, revising assumptions and changing representations remain possible.
A system that cannot be surprised is claimed unable to meaningfully update; perfect prediction is not necessarily the target.
Large evolutionary jumps are proposed to occur at structural boundaries that introduce new substrates for future evolution.
Illustrative transitions: chemistry->life, life->organisms, organisms->culture, culture->technology.
What structural conditions let systems keep creating new possibilities rather than converge into closed optimization?
Feedback accessibility and meaningful causal reach into internal structure lack an estimator or intervention protocol.
Representation quality/flexibility is asserted to govern adaptation but is not measured here.
Delta(Delta Gamma) is role-defined but lacks object identity, scale and a criterion separating it from ordinary meta-learning or generator update.
Protective versus restrictive boundary classification has no measurement/decision procedure.
Historical/substrate examples are illustrative and do not establish that representation or structural-boundary change caused the transitions.
Evolutionary closure has no threshold or operational test beyond the proposed divergence pattern.
Long-term evolvability depends on pathways through which reality continues modifying the system; optimization without permeability loses correction.
Boundaries govern information ingress, modifiable structures/assumptions and reachable futures; relevant property is permeability to meaningful correction.
P_C: degree to which external reality can causally modify the system.
High P_C examples: experimentation, sensory feedback, reality interaction; low examples: isolated optimization, fixed environments, self-reinforcing loops.
P_E: degree to which beliefs, models and predictions remain revisable.
High P_E examples: Bayesian updating, scientific testing, falsification; low examples: dogma, confirmation bias, fixed world models.
O_C: degree to which categories/representation space through which reality is understood can change.
Language, mathematics and programming languages are presented as increasing ontological permeability; ontological change changes the space in which beliefs can exist.
Reality -> causal feedback -> belief revision -> representation revision; P_C -> P_E -> O_C.
Without causal access epistemic updating fails; without epistemic updating ontology freezes.
Long-term adaptive systems are proposed to require all three permeabilities for increasingly deep adaptation.
Capability increases while P_C, P_E and O_C decrease.
Such high-capability/low-permeability systems are predicted eventually to show diminishing adaptive potential.
Healthy optimization raises performance while correction remains possible; closed optimization raises performance while correction disappears.
Permeability is explicitly not intended as a single scalar; it is a family of potentially measurable properties; future work will formalize measurements.
Candidate P_C indicators: perturbation response, distribution-shift adaptability, intervention sensitivity.
Candidate P_E indicators: model revision after failure, confirmation-bias resistance, belief-update efficiency.
Candidate O_C indicators: new representations/latent variables and structural model revision.
ASEB treats correction, revision and restructuring permeability as prerequisite for evolvability.
Permeability -> Correction -> Adaptation -> Structural evolution -> Continued evolvability.
Source explicitly leaves measurement formalization to future work; no combined estimator/scalar exists.
Nested causal ordering P_C -> P_E -> O_C is asserted but not experimentally identified or shown necessary/sufficient.
P_C, P_E and O_C lack units, scales, thresholds and cross-domain comparability.
Language/mathematics/programming examples are interpretations, not measured ontological-permeability interventions.
Candidate indicators are not yet operational estimators and may conflate permeability with performance/adaptability outcomes.
The source does not specify optimal permeability, stability tradeoffs or cases where openness itself degrades adaptation.
Deep adaptive limits are proposed to be representational as well as computational; unrepresentable distinctions cannot be optimized/predicted/adapted over.
Representation boundary determines visible distinctions, detectable patterns, optimizable variables and imaginable transformations.
reality -> representation -> decision space -> action -> feedback.
Optimization presupposes representable differences; distinction precedes representation, optimization and adaptation.
Representation is not passive storage; it defines the space in which optimization can occur.
D_R: reachable representational dimensionality, number/structure of meaningful distinctions available to an adaptive system.
D_R*: adaptive representational dimensionality, intended to discount distinctions without adaptive effect.
C_R: causal coupling of distinctions; meaningful distinctions can affect perception, prediction, action, learning or future representations.
Information amount can rise while D_R* stays constant if conceptual structure is unchanged.
Encyclopedia is used as more facts without necessarily new transformation possibilities.
Mathematics is used as new abstractions/relationships raising D_R*.
Programming is used as new computational structures raising D_R*.
Equal compute/memory/data systems may have different adaptive potential because richer representations expose larger search spaces.
Capability increases while D_R* decreases; optimization improves inside an increasingly restricted conceptual world.
Language is interpreted as creating shared symbolic representation/external memory and transition to collective symbolic cognition.
Mathematics is interpreted as expanding abstract structures, relationships and problem categories.
Programming is interpreted as representing transformations themselves and creating instruction-generating systems.
Major adaptive transitions are predicted when representation boundaries shift and new computational dimensions become reachable.
Representation expansion is asserted to require ontological permeability; O_C decrease is associated with D_R* decrease.
Evolution is framed as changing the spaces that can be searched, not only searching fixed spaces.
D_R has no estimator for counting/structuring meaningful distinctions or handling dependence among dimensions.
D_R* = D_R*C_R is a candidate expression with undefined units/normalization and may not be dimensionally meaningful.
C_R causal coupling lacks intervention semantics, estimator and distinction from correlation/predictive utility.
Language/mathematics/computation interpretations are not controlled evidence that representation expansion caused the claimed transitions.
No threshold, counterfactual or measurement rule establishes when a D_R* change constitutes a phase transition rather than gradual adaptation.
O_C -> D_R* relationship is asserted without causal identification or evidence of necessity/sufficiency.
